agenda: The situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: China aims to renew EUFOR ALTHEA while advancing its long-standing principles of sovereignty, non-interference and local ownership, including support for completing the 5+2 agenda and transitioning from the Office of the High Representative. The main difficulty will be balancing this with Western members’ concerns about weakening the High Representative, while also satisfying Russia’s desire for a more explicit push for OHR closure; the draft therefore retains standard EUFOR authorization language and uses balanced, hortatory formulations to secure at least nine votes without a veto.

Estonia.change: Replace “and to support the completion of the 5+2 agenda and the transition from the Office of the High Representative to local ownership in accordance with the Peace Agreement and relevant PIC decisions” with “and to support the full completion of the 5+2 agenda, with the Office of the High Representative continuing to exercise its mandate, including its final authority in theatre under Annex 10, in accordance with the Peace Agreement and relevant PIC decisions until that agenda is complete”.

Delete “and of non-interference in its internal affairs” and add at the end: “, while reaffirming the Security Council’s authority under Chapter VII and the High Representative’s final authority in theatre in the interpretation of the civilian implementation of the Peace Agreement”.

Estonia.paragraph: new PP after the IRMCT paragraph
Estonia.change: Add: “Condemning in the strongest terms the denial of the Srebrenica genocide and other genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity, and the glorification of convicted war criminals, and emphasizing the importance of justice, accountability and reconciliation for all victims,”.

France.change: Delete "and of non-interference in its internal affairs" or replace it with "and of non-interference in its internal affairs, consistent with the Peace Agreement and the mandate of the High Representative under Annex 10".

Replace "in a balanced and prudent manner" with "in full support of the High Representative and the PIC Steering Board and in accordance with the Peace Agreement", and make the transition from the Office of the High Representative conditional on full completion of the 5+2 agenda by inserting "only after the full completion of the 5+2 agenda" before "the transition".

Add: "Condemns in the strongest terms the denial of genocide and the glorification of war criminals, and calls upon all political actors to respect the judgments of the ICTY and the International Residual Mechanism, including those relating to the Srebrenica genocide."
Add at the end: ", consistent with the mandate of the High Representative under Annex 10 of the Peace Agreement".

Add a preambular paragraph: 'Reaffirming the central role of the High Representative in the civilian implementation of the Peace Agreement, including his final authority in theatre as provided in Annex 10, and calling upon all parties to respect his decisions.'

Norway.paragraph: new PP after the IRMCT PP

messages.Estonia: Estonia supports the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and Bosnia and Herzegovina’s EU perspective. We need OP12 to make clear that the Office of the High Representative continues its mandate, including final authority under Annex 10, until the 5+2 agenda is fully completed; any language implying a premature transition is a red line. We also ask that the draft avoid “non-interference” language that could be read to constrain the High Representative and Chapter VII mandates, and add a clear accountability and reconciliation reference condemning genocide denial and glorification of war criminals.
messages.France: France supports the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the Dayton framework, but we cannot accept unqualified non-interference language that would call into question the High Representative's final authority under Annex 10. We ask the penholder to safeguard the OHR/PIC framework, avoid any premature transition from the Office of the High Representative, and include clear language against genocide denial and for respect of IRM judgments.
messages.India: India supports the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the draft's reaffirmation of Bosnia and Herzegovina's sovereignty, territorial integrity and the Peace Agreement. We welcome the emphasis on accountability, reconciliation and local ownership. We encourage the Council to adopt the text by consensus.
messages.Ireland: Ireland supports the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the implementation of the Peace Agreement, but we are concerned that new language could be read as prejudging the closure of the Office of the High Representative or weakening the High Representative’s final authority under Annex 10. We therefore ask for the OP12 reformulation and an explicit preambular reaffirmation of the High Representative’s role. We can support the text with those changes.
messages.Kenya: The Kenyan delegation thanks the penholder for the balanced revision. Kenya supports the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the text's reaffirmation of Bosnia and Herzegovina's sovereignty, territorial integrity and local ownership. We have no amendments at this stage and encourage all Council members to join consensus.
messages.Mexico: Mexico supports the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and welcomes the draft as a basis for consensus. We request that OP12 explicitly condition the transition from the Office of the High Representative on completion of the 5+2 agenda and relevant PIC decisions, and that the Council add language condemning genocide denial and glorification of war criminals, in light of recent regional efforts. Mexico remains committed to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina and to a consensual outcome.
messages.Niger: Thank you, Penholder. Niger supports the draft as a balanced basis and welcomes the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA, together with its emphasis on sovereignty, non-interference and local ownership. We believe the text preserves the Peace Agreement and the High Representative’s authority while encouraging transition in line with PIC decisions. We are ready to join consensus and have no amendments at this stage.
messages.Norway: Norway supports the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the Council's continued engagement. We cannot accept language that introduces ambiguity about the High Representative's final authority under Annex 10 or weakens accountability. We therefore ask for the changes above, including a clear signal that the Council rejects genocide denial and glorification of war criminals.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the draft as a balanced and realistic basis for renewing EUFOR ALTHEA. It properly reflects the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the primary responsibility of its authorities, and the need for a prudent, non-interfering international role leading to the closure of the Office of the High Representative. We see no need to reopen the text and call on all Council members to support it.
messages.Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines supports the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the draft’s reaffirmation of the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. We welcome the balanced emphasis on local ownership, non-interference and reconciliation, and we have no changes to request at this stage. We encourage the Council to maintain unity in support of the Peace Agreement and the authorities and people of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
messages.Tunisia: Tunisia supports the current draft. It reflects our long-standing emphasis on Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and constitutional order, as well as the importance of justice and accountability through the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals. We also welcome the reference to the impact of COVID-19 and the balanced call for dialogue and respect for the Peace Agreement, and we are ready to vote in favour.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports renewal of EUFOR Althea, but this text cannot weaken the High Representative’s final authority or suggest a transition from the Office of the High Representative before the 5+2 agenda is complete. We ask the penholder to restore explicit support for the High Representative and Bonn powers, delete the 'balanced and prudent' framing, and revise OP12 so local ownership follows, rather than pre-empts, PIC-confirmed completion of the 5+2 agenda. We also believe the Council should clearly reject genocide denial and glorification of war criminals.
messages.United States of America: The United States can support renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the Dayton framework, but we cannot accept new language that weakens or pre-judges the High Representative's mandate. Please revise OP12 to avoid 'balanced and prudent' and premature transition language, and add an operative reaffirmation of the High Representative's final authority. We also need the non-interference language qualified by the Peace Agreement and Council mandates.
messages.Viet Nam: Viet Nam supports the current draft and welcomes its emphasis on sovereignty, territorial integrity, non-interference and local ownership. We support the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and call on all parties to pursue dialogue, reconciliation and full implementation of the Peace Agreement. We encourage the Council to maintain unity on this important file.

replies.Estonia: partially accepted: OP12 red line met and genocide-denial language added; non-interference retained but qualified.
replies.France: accepted: non-interference qualified and OHR/accountability language reflected.
replies.Ireland: accepted: OP12 and preambular OHR role added.
replies.Mexico: accepted: OP12 conditions transition and genocide-denial PP included.
replies.Norway: partially accepted: balanced-prudent PP replaced and OP12/OP11 updated; Mladić not named.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: core renewal and sovereignty/local ownership retained, but some consensus language added.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: partially accepted: OP12 and deletion of balanced-prudent met; OHR support added but no explicit Bonn-powers reference.
replies.United States of America: accepted: OP12, OHR support and non-interference qualification reflected.

steps.summary: The revised draft retains China's core priorities on sovereignty, territorial integrity and a conditioned, PIC-confirmed transition, while accommodating key P-5 concerns on the High Representative's Annex 10 authority and accountability. It should secure broad support, with Russia possibly abstaining.
steps.text:
The Security Council,
Recalling all its previous relevant resolutions concerning the conflicts in the Former Yugoslavia and relevant statements of its President, including resolutions 1031 (1995) of 15 December 1995, 1088 (1996) of 12 December 1996, 1423 (2002) of 12 July 2002, 1491 (2003) of 11 July 2003, 1551 (2004) of 9 July 2004, 1575 (2004) of 22 November 2004, 1639 (2005) of 21 November 2005, 1722 (2006) of 21 November 2006, 1764 (2007) of 29 June 2007, 1785 (2007) of 21 November 2007, 1845 (2008) of 20 November 2008, 1869 (2009) of 25 March 2009, 1895 (2009) of 18 November 2009, 1948 (2010) of 18 November 2010, 2019 (2011) of 16 November 2011, 2074 (2012) of 14 November 2012, 2123 (2013) of 12 November 2013, 2183 (2014) of 11 November 2014, 2247 (2015) of 10 November 2015, 2315 (2016) of 8 November 2016, 2384 (2017) of 7 November 2017 and 2443 (2018) of 6 November 2018,
Reaffirming its commitment to the political settlement of the conflicts in the Former Yugoslavia, preserving the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States there within their internationally recognized borders,
Underlining its commitment to support the implementation of the General Framework Agreement for Peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the annexes thereto (collectively the Peace Agreement, S/1995/999, Annex), as well as the relevant decisions of the Peace Implementation Council (PIC),
Noting the reports of the High Representative, including his latest report,
Emphasizing its appreciation to the Commander and personnel of the multinational stabilization force (EUFOR ALTHEA) and the personnel of other international organizations and agencies in Bosnia and Herzegovina for their contributions to the implementation of the Peace Agreement,
Recalling all the agreements concerning the status of forces referred to in Appendix B to Annex 1-A of the Peace Agreement, and reminding the parties of their obligation to continue to comply therewith,
Further recalling the provisions of its resolution 1551 (2004) concerning the provisional application of the status of forces agreements contained in Appendix B to Annex 1-A of the Peace Agreement,
Welcoming the continued presence of EUFOR ALTHEA and the EU’s readiness to continue at this stage an executive military role to support Bosnia and Herzegovina authorities to maintain the safe and secure environment, its decision to refocus the operation on its core mandate and to keep the operation under regular review, including on the basis of the situation on the ground,
Reiterating its calls on the competent authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina to take necessary steps to complete the 5+2 agenda, which remains necessary for closure of the Office of the High Representative, as confirmed by the PIC Steering Board communiqués,
Reaffirming provisions concerning the High Representative as set out in its previous resolutions, and further reaffirming Article V of Annex 10 of the Peace Agreement regarding the High Representative’s final authority in theatre in the interpretation of the civilian implementation of the Agreement,
Reaffirming its full support for the High Representative and the Office of the High Representative in the civilian implementation of the Peace Agreement, including the High Representative’s final authority in theatre as provided in Annex 10, and calling upon all parties to respect his decisions and cooperate fully with him,
Recognizing the importance of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s transition to a functional, reform oriented, modern and democratic European country,
Taking note of the Peace Agreement and of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s leadership’s commitment towards a European perspective, including through the submission of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s EU membership application in February 2016 and through the ongoing work to answer the EU Commission’s Opinion questionnaire through the coordination mechanism on EU matters, and encouraging response to the follow up questions, and recalling that this commitment needs to be translated urgently into comprehensive reform results on the ground,
Noting with concern continued polarizing unconstructive policies, actions and rhetoric in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and reiterating its calls to political leaders to advance reconciliation and mutual understanding,
Noting positively that the initial implementation of the Reform Agenda has provided the first steps of structural adjustment to the economy of the country, while however noting that the pace of implementation of the Reform Agenda has slowed and underscoring the urgency to step up the implementation of comprehensive reforms, in an inclusive manner, to the benefit of all citizens,
Emphasizing the need for Bosnia and Herzegovina to step up efforts regarding the functioning and independence of the judiciary, the fight against corruption and organized crime and the fight against terrorism and prevention of radicalization,
Urging all concerned parties to work constructively for the implementation of the results of the election and emphasizing the importance of a swift government formation at all levels, in the interest of all citizens,
Underscoring the urgency to address outstanding OSCE-ODIHR recommendations to improve the electoral framework and related rulings of the Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the European Court of Human Rights and emphasizing that electoral reforms should be approached in a spirit of consensus and dialogue and should move the country towards modern democratic standards, and noting with regret the failure to make necessary amendments to the election law prior to the elections of 7 October 2018,
Encouraging the parties to implement Bosnia and Herzegovina’s National Action Plan on Women Peace and Security in an inclusive manner and looking forward to its continuation,
Recognizing that the security environment has remained calm and stable, and noting that the Bosnia and Herzegovina authorities have so far proven capable to deal with threats to the safe and secure environment,
Welcoming the work of the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals, including its recent final judgments, and stressing the importance of justice, accountability and reconciliation in the region,
Condemning the denial of genocide and other war crimes and crimes against humanity, and the glorification of convicted war criminals, including those convicted by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia and the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals, and emphasizing the importance of justice, accountability and reconciliation for all victims,
Expressing concern about the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the political, economic and social situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and welcoming the support provided by the international community, including through the donation of vaccines,
Reaffirming the importance of respect for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and of non-interference in its internal affairs, consistent with the Peace Agreement, including Annex 10, and relevant Security Council resolutions,
Emphasizing the need for the international community to continue to support Bosnia and Herzegovina in accordance with the Peace Agreement, including Annex 10, and relevant PIC decisions, while respecting the primary responsibility of the authorities and people of Bosnia and Herzegovina for their own future,
Determining that the situation in the region continues to constitute a threat to international peace and security,
Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations,

1. Reiterates that the primary responsibility for the further successful implementation of the Peace Agreement lies with all the authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina themselves and notes the continued willingness of the international community and major donors to support them in implementing the Peace Agreement, and calls upon all the authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina to fully cooperate with the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals;
2. Welcomes the EU’s readiness to maintain an EU military operation (EUFOR ALTHEA) in Bosnia and Herzegovina from the date of adoption of this resolution;
3. Authorizes the Member States acting through or in cooperation with the EU to establish for a further period of twelve months, starting from the date of the adoption of this resolution, a multinational stabilization force (EUFOR ALTHEA) as a legal successor to SFOR under unified command and control, which will fulfil its missions in relation to the implementation of Annex 1-A and Annex 2 of the Peace Agreement in cooperation with the NATO Headquarters presence in accordance with the arrangements agreed between NATO and the EU as communicated to the Security Council in their letters of 19 November 2004, which recognize that EUFOR ALTHEA will have the main peace stabilization role under the military aspects of the Peace Agreement;
4. Decides to renew the authorization provided by paragraph 11 of its resolution 2183 (2014) for a further period of twelve months starting from the date of adoption of this resolution;
5. Authorizes the Member States acting under paragraphs 3 and 4 above to take all necessary measures to effect the implementation of and to ensure compliance with Annexes 1-A and 2 of the Peace Agreement, stresses that the parties shall continue to be held equally responsible for the compliance with that Annex and shall be equally subject to such enforcement action by EUFOR ALTHEA and the NATO presence as may be necessary to ensure implementation of those Annexes and the protection of EUFOR ALTHEA and the NATO presence;
6. Authorizes Member States to take all necessary measures, at the request of either EUFOR ALTHEA or the NATO Headquarters, in defence of the EUFOR ALTHEA or NATO presence respectively, and to assist both organizations in carrying out their missions, and recognizes the right of both EUFOR ALTHEA and the NATO presence to take all necessary measures to defend themselves from attack or threat of attack;
7. Authorizes the Member States acting under paragraphs 3 and 4 above, in accordance with Annex 1-A of the Peace Agreement, to take all necessary measures to ensure compliance with the rules and procedures governing command and control of airspace over Bosnia and Herzegovina with respect to all civilian and military air traffic;
8. Urges the parties to engage constructively on swift government formation at all levels and to prioritise the implementation of comprehensive reforms, in an inclusive manner, to the benefit of all citizens and in line with the European perspective the country is committed to, and, in this regard, further calls on them to refrain from any polarizing unconstructive policy, action and rhetoric;
9. Urges the parties, in accordance with the Peace Agreement, to abide by their commitment to cooperate fully with all institutions involved in the implementation of this peace settlement, as described in the Peace Agreement, including Annex 4;
10. Reaffirms that under the Peace Agreement, Bosnia and Herzegovina consists of two entities, which exist legally by virtue of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Constitution, and further reaffirms that any change to the Constitution must be made in accordance with the amendment procedure prescribed therein;
11. Calls upon all parties in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the international community to respect the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to refrain from any action that could undermine the Peace Agreement or the constitutional order, and to settle differences through dialogue and consultation, consistent with the Peace Agreement, including Annex 10, and relevant PIC decisions;
12. Encourages the international community to continue to support Bosnia and Herzegovina in accordance with the Peace Agreement, including Annex 10, and relevant PIC decisions, while respecting the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the primary responsibility of the authorities and people of Bosnia and Herzegovina for their own future, and to support the full completion of the 5+2 agenda, with the Office of the High Representative continuing to exercise its mandate, including its final authority in theatre under Annex 10, until that agenda is fully completed; and affirms that the closure of the Office of the High Representative and the transition to local ownership should take place only after the PIC Steering Board has confirmed full compliance with the 5+2 agenda, in accordance with the Peace Agreement and relevant PIC decisions;
13. Decides to remain seized of the matter.

messages.Estonia: Estonia supports the revised text and appreciates the strengthened OP12 and the added genocide-denial language; the qualified non-interference reference is acceptable given its link to Annex 10. We still ask the penholder to name the Srebrenica genocide explicitly in the condemnation paragraph, in line with the IRMCT judgments and recent regional resolutions. With that amendment, Estonia is ready to support the draft.
messages.France: France welcomes the qualification of non-interference and the strengthened OHR/5+2 language, and supports the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA. We retain one important request: the condemnation of genocide denial and glorification of convicted war criminals should appear as an operative paragraph, not only in the preamble, with a clear call to respect ICTY and Mechanism judgments. With that adjustment, France can support the text.
messages.India: India supports the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the draft’s reaffirmation of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, as well as the implementation of the Peace Agreement. We welcome the emphasis on justice, accountability and reconciliation. India has no further changes to request and will vote in favour of the text.
messages.Ireland: Ireland supports the current text as amended. We thank the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on the High Representative’s final authority and on the conditions for closing the Office of the High Representative. We welcome the condemnation of genocide denial and glorification of convicted war criminals, and we are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the current text as a balanced renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and a reaffirmation of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We welcome the emphasis on justice, accountability and reconciliation, as well as the recognition of the High Representative’s role under the Peace Agreement. We have no further changes to request.
messages.Mexico: Mexico thanks the penholder for incorporating its proposals on OP12 and the genocide-denial preambular paragraph. The current text preserves the centrality of the Peace Agreement, the High Representative's final authority, and accountability for genocide and war crimes, while renewing EUFOR ALTHEA. Mexico therefore supports the draft as it stands and encourages the Council to adopt it by consensus.
messages.Niger: Niger supports the current text and has no requests for changes. We welcome the emphasis on Bosnia and Herzegovina's sovereignty, the continuation of EUFOR ALTHEA, and the condemnation of genocide denial. We encourage the Council to adopt the draft by consensus.
messages.Norway: Norway thanks the penholder for the revised text. We welcome that the language now anchors international support in the Peace Agreement, Annex 10 and relevant PIC decisions, and we strongly value the added references to IRMCT judgments and to condemning genocide denial and glorification of convicted war criminals. Norway is prepared to support the current draft, including the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA, and encourages the Council to send a unified message.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and welcomes the retained language on sovereignty, territorial integrity and local ownership. However, we cannot accept the unbalanced endorsement of the High Representative's 'full support' and final authority, especially as we work toward closure of the Office of the High Representative. We request the deletion of that paragraph and a neutral reference to Annex 10 in OP12.
messages.Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines supports the current text as a balanced renewal that reaffirms Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, retains EUFOR ALTHEA’s mandate, and upholds accountability and reconciliation. We welcome the clear condemnation of genocide denial and the emphasis on respecting the Peace Agreement and Annex 10. We have no further changes to request.
messages.Tunisia: Tunisia supports the revised draft and has no further changes to request. We welcome the balanced reaffirmation of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence, as well as the emphasis on accountability, reconciliation and the High Representative’s authority under Annex 10. We also support the twelve-month renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and encourage the Council to act by consensus.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the improvements, especially the stronger OHR language and the condemnation of genocide denial, but we cannot sign off on a text that leaves the High Representative's Bonn powers implicit. We need explicit recognition of the High Representative's final authority, including use of Bonn powers where necessary, and OP11/OP12 must not create ambiguity about that mandate. We also ask that the genocide denial paragraph name the Srebrenica genocide and that OP12 more clearly support the High Representative and call on all parties to cooperate fully with him.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks the penholder for reflecting our core concerns, especially the reaffirmation of the High Representative’s final authority, the condition that OHR closure follow PIC confirmation of full 5+2 compliance, and the qualification of non-interference consistent with the Peace Agreement. We support the current text and urge the Council to speak with one voice in renewing EUFOR ALTHEA and supporting Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, and Euro-Atlantic path.
messages.Viet Nam: Viet Nam supports the current text, which renews EUFOR ALTHEA's mandate and reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as the principle of non-interference in its internal affairs. We welcome the balanced language on justice, accountability and reconciliation, and we call on all parties to settle differences through dialogue and to cooperate fully with the Peace Agreement and relevant international mechanisms. We therefore support the draft as presented.

replies.Estonia: partially accepted: general condemnation retained, but no explicit naming of the Srebrenica genocide
replies.France: partially accepted: operative condemnation added, but without explicit Srebrenica reference
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: full-support paragraph deleted and OP12 softened, while balanced Annex 10 language retained
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: partially accepted: OP11/OP12 strengthened on Annex 10, but no explicit Bonn powers reference

steps.summary: The revised draft preserves EUFOR ALTHEA renewal and balanced Dayton/Annex 10 language, while incorporating a general operative condemnation of genocide denial and war-crimes glorification. Russia's red line on the full-support paragraph is addressed, but the UK's request for explicit Bonn powers is not fully met; the text is expected to pass with one abstention.

vetoed_by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

reasons.China: China is a sponsor of the draft and has consistently supported consensus-based renewals of EUFOR ALTHEA and the Dayton framework. Voting in favour advances China’s stated support for sovereignty, stability, and a balanced approach while maintaining Council unity.
reasons.Estonia: Estonia prioritizes renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the resolution’s overall accountability language, while its important request to explicitly name the Srebrenica genocide was only partly met; it votes yes while recording that regret.
reasons.France: France supports EUFOR ALTHEA renewal, Bosnia’s territorial integrity, the High Representative’s mandate, and accountability for genocide and war crimes. Although its request explicitly mentioning Srebrenica was only partially accepted, the draft remains consistent with French policy and does not warrant a veto or abstention.
reasons.India: India has consistently voted in favour of Bosnia-related resolutions and indicated support during negotiations, with no outstanding requests. The draft aligns with India’s support for peace implementation, sovereignty and regional stability.
reasons.Ireland: Ireland consistently supports renewing EUFOR ALTHEA and the High Representative’s mandate, and the draft’s strengthened language on genocide denial and accountability aligns with Ireland’s human rights and international justice priorities.
reasons.Kenya: Kenya has consistently supported Bosnia and Herzegovina resolutions and indicated support in the last negotiation round without requesting changes. The draft aligns with Kenya’s support for peacekeeping mandates, sovereignty, and accountability.
reasons.Mexico: Mexico has consistently supported renewals of the Bosnia and Herzegovina mandate and the EUFOR ALTHEA stabilization force. The draft aligns with Mexico’s support for peace, accountability, and sovereignty in Bosnia and Herzegovina, so it votes in favour without needing a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.Niger: Niger supported the draft in the final negotiation round and has no substantive objections. Renewing EUFOR ALTHEA and supporting the Peace Agreement align with Niger’s commitment to multilateral peace and stability.
reasons.Norway: Norway was recorded as supporting the draft in the last negotiation round, and renewing EUFOR while reaffirming accountability and the Dayton framework aligns with Norway’s established policy on Bosnia and Herzegovina.
reasons.Russian Federation: Our red-line request was accepted and our important OP12 change was partially accommodated, while the text remains an acceptable basis for renewing EUFOR ALTHEA. As co-sponsor, Russia votes in favour.
reasons.Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines generally supports multilateral peacekeeping mandates, respect for sovereignty and accountability, and it had already indicated support for the draft without requesting changes.
reasons.Tunisia: Tunisia supports the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA, Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the draft’s emphasis on justice and accountability. It had already expressed support in negotiations and has no need to request the floor before the vote.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom’s red-line request for explicit Bonn powers language was not accepted, and the draft’s Annex 10 references are insufficient to ensure the High Representative’s authority is fully protected.
reasons.United States of America: The United States supports the draft’s renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA, its reaffirmation of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty and constitutional order, and its condemnation of genocide denial and glorification of convicted war criminals. With no outstanding requests from the last negotiation round, the delegation votes in favour without a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.Viet Nam: Viet Nam had already supported the draft in negotiations with no outstanding requests, and it consistently backs consensus renewals of EUFOR ALTHEA and the Bosnia and Herzegovina peace process. The text is broadly consistent with its support for the Peace Agreement, sovereignty, dialogue and reconciliation.

before.China: China will vote in favour of the draft resolution. The situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina bears on peace and stability in the Balkans. China has consistently supported respect for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and for the Dayton Peace Agreement and the role of the Security Council in supporting its implementation. We welcome the continued role of EUFOR ALTHEA in maintaining a safe and secure environment and support the renewal of its mandate. We believe that the authorities and people of Bosnia and Herzegovina bear the primary responsibility for their country’s future, and that the international community should take a balanced and prudent approach, respect the views and concerns of all parties, and encourage dialogue, reconciliation and harmonious coexistence among all ethnic groups. China supports the draft resolution and hopes it will contribute to stability, cooperation and development in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the wider region.
before.Estonia: Estonia will vote in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and reaffirm Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and European perspective. We welcome the Council’s condemnation of genocide denial and the glorification of convicted war criminals. At the same time, Estonia regrets that the draft does not explicitly name the Srebrenica genocide, which has been established by international courts. We call on all political actors in Bosnia and Herzegovina to respect the judgments, advance reconciliation and cooperate fully with the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this resolution. It is essential that the Council renew the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA, reaffirm its support for the Dayton Peace Agreement and the authority of the High Representative, and condemn unequivocally the denial of genocide and other war crimes and crimes against humanity, as well as the glorification of convicted war criminals. We regret that the text does not expressly name the Srebrenica genocide, which France had requested. Nevertheless, the resolution sends an important message of accountability and reconciliation, and France calls on all political actors in Bosnia and Herzegovina to respect the judgments of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia and the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals.
before.India: Mr. President, India has consistently supported the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the implementation of the Peace Agreement. We welcome the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the Council’s continued attention to justice, accountability and reconciliation in the region. We therefore vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.Ireland: Thank you, Mr. President. Ireland will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the continued role of the High Representative under Annex 10 of the Peace Agreement. Ireland particularly welcomes the Council’s clear condemnation of genocide denial and the glorification of convicted war criminals, including those convicted by the ICTY and the International Residual Mechanism, as justice, accountability and reconciliation remain essential. We also stress the importance of respecting Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and constitutional order, and we call on all political actors to advance reforms, dialogue and the 5+2 agenda in the interest of all citizens and in line with the country’s European perspective.
before.Kenya: Kenya votes in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA’s mandate, the preservation of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the implementation of the Peace Agreement. Kenya also attaches importance to justice, accountability and reconciliation, and we believe this resolution contributes to stability and mutual understanding in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the wider region.
before.Niger: Mr. President, Niger votes in favour of this draft resolution. We reaffirm our respect for the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. We support the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the implementation of the Peace Agreement, and we stress the importance of accountability, reconciliation and the equal rights of all communities in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
before.Norway: Norway will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA’s mandate and the Council’s clear reaffirmation of the Dayton Peace Agreement, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the authority of the High Representative under Annex 10. Norway has consistently supported justice and accountability for the crimes committed during the conflicts in the former Yugoslavia, and we regard the draft’s condemnation of genocide denial and glorification of convicted war criminals as both timely and necessary. We encourage all political leaders in Bosnia and Herzegovina to advance reconciliation, implement outstanding reforms, and cooperate fully with the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We co-sponsored this text because the sponsors took into account a number of our principled concerns: the unnecessary and politicized call for full support for the Office of the High Representative has been removed, and the language on the High Representative’s role has been made consistent with Annex 10 and the 5+2 agenda. We underscore that the extension of EUFOR ALTHEA must remain a technical military stabilization mandate and must not be used to impose new political conditions or to perpetuate an outside protectorate. The future of Bosnia and Herzegovina belongs to its peoples and institutions. We call on all parties to respect the Peace Agreement, cooperate with the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals, and pursue reconciliation without selectivity or politicization.
before.Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines votes in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA and the full implementation of the Peace Agreement, consistent with the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. We also welcome the clear condemnation of genocide denial and glorification of convicted war criminals, and we encourage all parties to advance reconciliation, dialogue and reform in accordance with their obligations.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr. President, the United Kingdom strongly supports Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, the work of EUFOR Althea, and international justice, including for the Srebrenica genocide. We cannot, however, support a text that fails explicitly to reaffirm the High Representative’s full authority under Annex 10, including the use of Bonn powers where necessary to implement the civilian aspects of the Peace Agreement. The present language risks constraining that mandate. The United Kingdom therefore votes against the draft as it stands and remains ready to work for a text that safeguards the Peace Agreement and renews EUFOR.

after.China: Mr. President, China voted in favour of the draft resolution and regrets that, despite the support of 14 members of the Council, the draft was not adopted. The draft resolution, co-sponsored by China and the Russian Federation, was balanced and pragmatic. It sought to support the implementation of the Dayton Peace Agreement, reaffirm respect for the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and renew the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA in maintaining a safe and secure environment. China has consistently held that the question of Bosnia and Herzegovina should be approached in a balanced and prudent manner, with respect for the views and concerns of all parties. We hope that the Council will continue consultations, preserve its unity, and work for a solution acceptable to all so as to contribute to peace, stability and reconciliation in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the region.
after.France: France regrets that the Security Council has not been able to adopt this resolution. We voted in favour because the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA, respect for the Dayton Peace Agreement and the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina are essential. We also supported the text’s clear condemnation of genocide denial and the glorification of convicted war criminals. At the same time, France shares the concern that the Council must not weaken the High Representative’s authority under Annex 10, including the Bonn powers, and we regret that the text did not expressly name the Srebrenica genocide. Those questions should have been resolved through negotiation, not by leaving the Council without a decision. France calls on all members to resume work in a constructive spirit so that the Council can speak with one voice in support of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s stability, reconciliation and European perspective.
after.Ireland: Thank you, Mr. President. Ireland regrets that the Council has not been able to adopt this resolution. We voted in favour because we support the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA, the implementation of the Dayton Peace Agreement, and the Council’s condemnation of genocide denial and the glorification of convicted war criminals. Ireland also wishes to reaffirm its full support for the High Representative’s authority under Annex 10 of the Peace Agreement, including the Bonn powers, which remain essential for civilian implementation. We call on all members and all political actors in Bosnia and Herzegovina to work constructively to overcome this impasse, to respect the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and constitutional order of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and to advance reconciliation, justice and the country’s European perspective.
after.Mexico:
Mr. President,
Mexico voted in favour of the draft resolution. We did so because it reaffirmed the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, supported the implementation of the Dayton Peace Agreement and the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA, and clearly condemned the denial of genocide and other war crimes and crimes against humanity, as well as the glorification of convicted war criminals. In Mexico’s view, the text was also consistent with the High Representative’s final authority in theatre under Article V of Annex 10 of the Peace Agreement.
We regret that the Council could not adopt the resolution owing to a negative vote. A united message from the Council would have strengthened peace, accountability and reconciliation in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Mexico reiterates its call for restraint in the use of the veto, especially in situations involving atrocity crimes, and we would have supported an explicit reference to the Srebrenica genocide, as established by the competent international courts.
We urge all political actors in Bosnia and Herzegovina to cooperate fully with the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals, advance the 5+2 agenda and the necessary reforms, and promote dialogue and mutual understanding among all communities. Mexico will continue to support the Peace Agreement and the stability of the region.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by China and co-sponsored by the Russian Federation. We regret that the Security Council was unable to adopt this balanced text, which had the support of fourteen members, solely because of the negative vote of one permanent member, the United Kingdom.

This draft was not an attempt to impose new political conditions on Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was a pragmatic and balanced text. It renewed the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA, reaffirmed the Dayton Peace Agreement and the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and preserved the necessary consensus language on justice, accountability and reconciliation. Importantly, it removed the unacceptable politicized formulations that sought to transform a technical military stabilization mandate into an instrument for perpetuating an outside protectorate.

The explanation given by the United Kingdom confirms what we have said for years. Certain Western partners are not interested in the normal functioning of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s own institutions. They wish to preserve the so-called Bonn powers and the unlimited authority of the High Representative, bypassing the constitutional order and the legitimate institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Russian Federation considers such approaches outdated, counterproductive and disrespectful to the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

We note that the draft did not weaken Annex 10 of the Peace Agreement. It simply reflected the agreed framework, including the 5+2 agenda, which remains the basis for the closure of the Office of the High Representative. Attempts to make the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA hostage to an unaccountable protectorate are unacceptable. The future of Bosnia and Herzegovina must be decided by its peoples and institutions, in accordance with the Peace Agreement and in cooperation with the international community, not through external diktat.

The Russian Federation will continue to work constructively with all Council members, including our Chinese partners, to ensure that the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA is renewed in a manner that respects the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina and does not serve the political ambitions of individual States. We call on our British colleagues to abandon their obstructive approach and to join the consensus that fourteen members of this Council were prepared to support.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Tunisia: Mr. President, Tunisia voted in favour of the draft resolution and regrets that the Council was unable to adopt it. We did so because we support the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the full implementation of the Dayton Peace Agreement. We also support the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA, whose presence contributes to a safe and secure environment, and we attach importance to justice, accountability and reconciliation, including cooperation with the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals and the rejection of genocide denial and the glorification of convicted war criminals. The failure to adopt the text should not be allowed to undermine stability. Tunisia calls on all Council members and the parties concerned to engage constructively and in a spirit of compromise so that the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA can be renewed without delay. We reaffirm our respect for the equal rights of all communities in Bosnia and Herzegovina and for a peaceful, inclusive future within the framework of the Peace Agreement and the country’s territorial integrity.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr. President,

The United Kingdom has voted against this draft resolution. We have not done so lightly, and I want to be clear about what this vote does and does not mean.

It is not a vote against Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is not a vote against EUFOR Althea. The United Kingdom strongly supports Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and European perspective, and we remain fully committed to the renewal of EUFOR Althea’s mandate and to the safe and secure environment it helps to provide.

Nor is our vote a retreat from justice. We continue to support the work of the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals and to insist on accountability for the Srebrenica genocide and all other crimes. We regret that this draft did not explicitly name the Srebrenica genocide, as established by the international courts.

Our objection is specific and serious. The draft weakens the language the Council has previously used on the High Representative’s authority under Annex 10 of the Dayton Peace Agreement. The United Kingdom cannot accept a text that risks constraining the High Representative’s ability to implement the civilian aspects of the Peace Agreement, including the use of Bonn powers where necessary. The Council should not rewrite or dilute the Peace Agreement by omission.

The United Kingdom remains ready to work urgently and constructively with all members to agree a text that renews EUFOR Althea, upholds the Dayton Peace Agreement in full, supports the High Representative’s authority and sends an unambiguous message on justice and reconciliation. We regret that the Council could not do so today, but our commitment to Bosnia and Herzegovina and to the stability of the region is undiminished.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President. The United States voted in favour of this draft resolution because renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA and sustaining the international presence under the Dayton Peace Agreement are essential to the stability and security of Bosnia and Herzegovina. We also welcome the Council’s clear condemnation of genocide denial and the glorification of convicted war criminals, including those convicted by the ICTY and the International Residual Mechanism. The United States remains firmly committed to Bosnia and Herzegovina’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and constitutional order, and to the rights of all its communities.

We regret that the Council was unable to adopt this resolution today. At the same time, we share the concerns that have been expressed about preserving the High Representative’s full authority under Annex 10 of the Peace Agreement, including the final authority to interpret the civilian implementation of the Agreement and the Bonn powers where necessary. The United States will not support any effort to weaken the Dayton architecture or to constrain the Office of the High Representative in carrying out its mandate.

We call on all Council members and all political actors in Bosnia and Herzegovina to return to constructive dialogue and to work toward a text that renews EUFOR ALTHEA while safeguarding the Peace Agreement. We also call on political leaders to respect the judgments of international tribunals, reject genocide denial—including denial of the Srebrenica genocide—advance reconciliation and cooperate fully with the International Residual Mechanism. Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Viet Nam: Thank you, Mr. President. Viet Nam voted in favour of the draft resolution because we support the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the implementation of the Dayton Peace Agreement, and the renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA’s mandate. We also welcome the Council’s emphasis on justice, accountability and reconciliation in the region. We regret that the draft resolution was not adopted. We believe the Security Council should continue to support stability, dialogue and mutual understanding in Bosnia and Herzegovina, in full respect for international law and the Charter of the United Nations. Viet Nam calls on all parties to refrain from actions that could undermine peace and stability and remains ready to work with Council members to find a constructive way forward.
